Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:00 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Mahiya Kabir, 78, female. Mrs. Kabir comes in reporting that her breathlessness has grown worse for several days, accompanied by more sputum than usual. She has a long history of smoking and mentions her symptoms flared after rubbish was burned near her home in Khilgaon. She works as a shopkeeper. She denies chest pain at rest or fever. On examination: SpO2 86%, BP 114/73 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 78 kg. Coarse crepitations and wheeze heard across both lung fields. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Rafiq Haque, 40, male. Mr. Haque returns for review regarding his ongoing headaches, describing a throbbing headache on one side and a strong need to lie in a dark room. He is a bank officer and notes the attacks have been worse since starting night shifts at a hospital in Old Dhaka, occurring about 9 headache days a month. He denies visual aura, vomiting, or weakness. On examination: BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 75 kg. Neurological examination is normal. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Champa Howlader, 62, female. Mrs. Howlader attends for her review, describing a heavy feeling in the chest that eases with rest within minutes, breathlessness on effort, and chest tightness when walking fast or climbing. She is a shopkeeper and states this was first felt while rushing to catch a train in Rampura. She denies palpitations, dizziness, or nocturnal dyspnoea. On examination: BP 157/85 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 90 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds; chest is clear. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Morium Begum, 72, female. Mrs. Begum returns for follow-up, reporting no current symptoms. She mentions a father who had a heart attack at 55 and high cholesterol found on a routine test during a pre-employment test in Sirajganj, with an LDL cholesterol of 4.9 mmol/L. She works as a farmer. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. On examination: BP 112/75 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 49 kg. Cardiovascular exam is entirely unremarkable. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Khadija Hasan, 55, female. Mrs. Hasan attends for review, reporting stiffness in the morning for a few minutes, knee pain on the stairs, and a creaking knee. She works as a textile engineer and mentions her joint discomfort has been worse since moving to a building with no lift in Barishal. She has Hypothyroidism. She denies joint locking, instability, or previous trauma. On examination: BMI 32.8, BP 124/79 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 47 kg. Both knees show mild crepitus and tenderness around the patella without significant effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Masud Pramanik, 52, male. Mr. Pramanik presents for his first visit with neck tightness and long hours at a screen. He works as a rickshaw puller and notes his symptoms are worse since long daily commutes in Tejgaon, presenting with a daily headache that is worst on waking after heavy painkiller use and a pain score of 3/10. He denies focal weakness or visual disturbances. On examination: BP 111/84 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 77 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and neck muscles show generalized tenderness. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Orin Khatun, 52, female. Mrs. Khatun visits for the first time complaining of a thick white discharge and soreness in the genital region. She works as an electrician and states the trouble started after a course of antibiotics taken in Shyamoli, with a random blood glucose of 7.0 mmol/L noted today. She denies fever, lower abdominal pain, or abnormal bleeding. On examination: BP 124/86 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 47 kg. Pelvic inspection reveals thick curdy discharge and mucosal erythema. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Taslima Talukder, 55, female. Mrs. Talukder attends for review, describing low mood for over three weeks and no interest in usual activities. She works as a madrasa teacher and explains that her symptoms began after moving away from family to Banani, characterized by sleeping too much and overeating rather than poor sleep, with a PHQ-9 score of 13. She denies psychotic symptoms. On examination: BP 113/84 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 67 kg. She appears subdued but cooperative. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 11:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Abdul Karim, 61, male. Mr. Karim returns for review, reporting cuts that heal slowly and losing weight without trying. He works as a cricket coach and notes these issues were found during a routine test before a trip to Wari, showing a fasting glucose of 7.6 mmol/L. He denies excessive thirst, blurred vision, or foot ulcers. On examination: BP 117/76 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 75 kg. Systemic examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check the feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 11:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Masud Rahman, 42, male. Mr. Rahman attends for a follow-up visit complaining of itchy eyes and symptoms that grow worse with dust. He works as a schoolteacher and notes his flares occur each spring in Narayanganj, experiencing about 15 sneezing fits a day. He has Bronchial asthma. He denies fever, facial pain, or epistaxis. On examination: BP 111/79 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 93 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy; throat is clear. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 11:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rina Dey, 51, female. Mrs. Dey comes in for review, describing a sour taste in her mouth and symptoms that worsen when lying down. She works as a textile engineer and notes her discomfort has been worse since a job change in Shyamoli meant late heavy dinners. She has Essential hypertension. She denies dysphagia, vomiting, or weight loss. On examination: BMI 28.1, BP 138/86 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 68 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 11:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Mahfuz Molla, 32, male. Mr. Molla attends for review, reporting that his symptoms are worse in winter, accompanied by itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees and scratching at night. He works as a photographer and states the condition is worse since switching to a strong detergent in Tejgaon, with an affected area about 9 cm across. He denies bleeding or blistering. On examination: BP 127/80 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 59 kg. Well-demarcated dry erythematous plaques with lichenification found over extensor surfaces. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 11:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Arifa Kabir, 43, female. Mrs. Kabir presents for her first visit complaining of burning when passing urine, a lower belly ache, and going to the toilet often. She works as an accountant and mentions the symptoms started after a trip to Old Dhaka, with a recorded temperature of 99.0°F. She has Essential hypertension. She denies loin pain, rigors, or visible haematuria. On examination: BP 149/86 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 49 kg. Suprapubic tenderness is present. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not hold urine for long. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 12:30 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Popy Sultana, 42, female. Mrs. Sultana returns for follow-up reporting cramping belly pain, stools that switch between loose and hard, and symptoms that become worse with stress. She works as an electrician and reports her trouble began after a bout of food poisoning in Narayanganj, with a pain score of 4/10. She denies rectal bleeding or unexplained weight loss. On examination: BP 110/86 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 58 kg. Abdomen is soft, non-tender on deep palpation, with normal bowel sounds. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 12:30 PM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sumaiya Faruque, 47, female. Mrs. Faruque attends for review, describing shaky hands, hating the heat, and losing weight despite eating well. She works as a bank officer and noticed these changes during a hot summer in Shyamoli. She denies visual changes, chest pain, or weakness. On examination: pulse 128 bpm, BP 114/79 mmHg, weight 76 kg. Fine tremor of outstretched hands and brisk reflexes noted; thyroid gland is diffusely enlarged. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Shikha Nath, 79, female. Mrs. Nath attends for review, reporting tingling like pins and needles, burning in both feet, and symptoms that are worse at night. She works as a farmer and explains her trouble started after years of high sugar found at a health camp in Barishal, showing reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites. She has Hypothyroidism. She denies motor weakness or unsteadiness of gait. On examination: BP 118/81 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 54 kg. Ankle jerks are absent bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 03:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Anwar Sarkar, 72, male. Mr. Sarkar visits for the first time complaining of numbness in the toes and symptoms that are worse at night. He works as a shopkeeper and notes his discomfort is worse since walking barefoot at home in Rangpur, presenting with reduced sensation at 8 of 10 monofilament test sites. He has Hypothyroidism. He denies pain in the calves on walking or sudden weakness. On examination: BP 133/81 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 85 kg. Vibration sense is impaired up to the ankles. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 03:30 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tanvir Dewan, 33, male. Mr. Dewan comes in for his first visit with bloating and cramping belly pain. He works as a garment merchandiser and notes his symptoms are worse since starting a high-pressure job in Gazipur, with a pain score of 5/10. He denies fever, vomiting, or altered bowel habits of recent acute onset. On examination: BP 114/83 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 77 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild lower quadrant tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 03:33 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Sanjida Faruque, 67, female. Mrs. Faruque attends for review, stating she is always feeling cold, has dry skin, and feels slow and tired. She is a retired civil servant and reports these findings were discovered during tests for tiredness after moving to Cox's Bazar, with a TSH of 16.7 mIU/L. She denies constipation or weight gain of sudden onset. On examination: BP 129/73 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 71 kg. Skin is cool and dry; deep tendon reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 04:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Shathi Bepari, 58, female. Mrs. Bepari returns for follow-up reporting night pain in the shoulder and being unable to raise the arm. She works as a software developer and states her condition began gradually after a long illness in Tongi, where her shoulder lifts only to 85 degrees. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies direct injury or joint swelling. On examination: BP 136/76 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 80 kg. Active and passive range of motion is markedly restricted in all directions. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 04:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Arif Mahmud, 56, male. Mr. Mahmud visits for the first time complaining of eye discomfort that is worse in air conditioning and long hours of screen time. He works as an NGO field officer and notes his symptoms are worse since moving to a new air-conditioned office in Rampura, with a tear break-up time of 7 seconds. He denies discharge, sudden vision loss, or eye pain. On examination: BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 93 kg. Conjunctiva is clear, and corneal surface shows punctate staining. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 04:30 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Khadija Dewan, 50, female. Mrs. Dewan attends for her first visit complaining of symptoms that are worse with dust and itchy eyes. She works as a lawyer and notes her condition is worse since keeping a cat at home in Bogura, experiencing about 6 sneezing fits a day. She denies fever, earache, or breathing difficulty. On examination: BP 120/72 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 59 kg. Nasal turbinates are swollen and pale; pharynx is clear. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-13 04:30 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Rezaul Mahmud, 44, male. He works as an office cleaner and explains his illness began after moving away from family to Gulshan, with a PHQ-9 score of 16. He denies suicidal ideation or hallucinations. On examination: BP 132/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 94 kg. Mood is depressed with restricted affect. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. Visit note | 2025-09-14 10:00 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Mehnaz Pramanik, 79, female. She works as a farmer and mentions her symptoms were first noticed while climbing to a fourth-floor flat in Tongi. She has Bronchial asthma. She denies orthopnoea or ankle swelling. Visit note | 2025-09-14 10:30 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Dipali Roy, 59, female. Mrs. Roy returns for review complaining of knee pain on the stairs and stiffness in the morning for a few minutes. She is a madrasa teacher and states her joint pain has been worse since moving to a building with no lift in Khulna. She denies locking, instability, or redness. On examination: BMI 29.2, BP 112/71 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 61 kg. Mild crepitus on knee flexion with no joint effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Visit note | 2025-09-14 11:30 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Sraboni Paul, 69, female. Mrs. Paul comes in for her ongoing review, explaining that she has noticed steady weight gain over recent months, alongside feeling exceptionally slow, constantly tired, and feeling cold all the time. She is a shopkeeper by trade and first became concerned when a cold winter in Keraniganj felt significantly harder to bear than usual. She reports wearing extra layers indoors and struggling with sluggishness during her daily routines at the market. She denies any chest pain, palpitations, changes in bowel habits, or sudden mood disturbances. On examination: TSH 13.1 mIU/L, BP 116/81 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm and regular, weight 69 kg. Her skin feels dry and cool to the touch, deep tendon reflexes show delayed relaxation phase, and there is no neck swelling or tenderness. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued to adjust her ongoing thyroid hormone replacement therapy. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up is scheduled in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 11:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Eva Khatun, 51, female. Mrs. Khatun attends for her initial evaluation, reporting itchy raised welts that appear unpredictably, fade away, and then reappear in different areas. She mentions that these troublesome symptoms started shortly after taking a new painkiller bought from a pharmacy in Tejgaon. She works as a restaurant cook and finds the constant itching quite distracting during her shifts. She denies any breathing difficulty, lip swelling, dizziness, or fever. On examination: about 30 welts on the trunk and arms, BP 134/78 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 80 kg. The lesions are erythematous, blanching, and annular without blistering or scarring. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued for antihistamines and a short-course topical treatment. She was advised to avoid the suspected painkiller, keep a detailed symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if her tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Shamima Siddique, 69, female. Mrs. Siddique returns for her routine review, reporting persistent numbness in her toes and an unpleasant tingling sensation like pins and needles in both feet. She works as a shopkeeper and noticed these sensory changes after enduring long hours standing on hard floors at a busy commercial space in Barishal. She takes her prescribed glucose-lowering medications for her underlying condition but admits compliance has occasionally slipped. She denies any sharp shooting pains, night-time leg cramps, or open sores on her feet. On examination: reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 112/86 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 74 kg. Ankle jerks are diminished bilaterally, and peripheral pulses are intact. Comorbidity: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued for neuropathic symptom management. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under strict control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 02:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Ashraf Hasan, 68, male. Mr. Hasan comes back for a review of his chronic respiratory symptoms, stating that his breathlessness has been noticeably worse for several days, accompanied by producing more sputum than usual and a long history of smoking. He works as a tailor and explains that his breathing difficulties worsened during the dusty dry season in Faridpur. He reports using his rescue inhaler more frequently over the past week. He denies chest pain, fever, or leg swelling. On examination: SpO2 91%, BP 130/80 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 93 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheezing and prolonged expiration, with no focal crackles. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued for adjusted bronchodilator therapy and a short course of oral corticosteroids. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke exposure, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Selim Khan, 69, male. Mr. Khan attends for a follow-up consultation regarding his joint complaints, noting persistent knee pain when climbing stairs and stiffness in the morning that lasts for a few minutes before easing. He is a farmer by occupation and mentions that his joint discomfort has become much worse since moving to a multi-story building with no lift in Noakhali. He denies any joint locking, sudden giving way, or severe night pain. On examination: BMI 29.2, BP 131/80 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 47 kg. Both knees show mild crepitus on movement, no significant joint effusion, and a full passive range of motion with mild discomfort at terminal flexion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued for mild analgesics and topical anti-inflammatory gel. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 02:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Asif Matubbar, 66, male. Mr. Matubbar returns for his psychiatric review, describing ongoing trouble falling asleep most nights and persistent worry about his lack of sleep. He works as a madrasa teacher and notes that his sleep disturbance began after starting rotating shifts at a manufacturing facility in Rampura. He reports feeling exhausted during daytime hours and frustrated by his inability to switch off his mind at bedtime. He denies depressive symptoms, suicidal thoughts, or substance abuse. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 19, BP 126/80 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 89 kg. He appears fatigued with mild psychomotor slowing. Comorbidity: Hypothyroidism. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued for short-term sleep support. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 02:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Dalia Sultana, 38, female. Mrs. Sultana attends for a follow-up evaluation, reporting that she keeps getting breathless on the stairs and has noticed she is looking pale. She works as an accountant and mentions her fatigue started after a severe stomach illness during an extended stay in Kushtia. Presentation note: she admits to a strange craving to chew ice and complains of a sore smooth tongue alongside her tiredness. She denies recent bleeding, chest pain, or fever. On examination: haemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, BP 133/78 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 82 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and her tongue appears smooth with papillary atrophy. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron supplementation. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 02:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Shamim Akand, 29, male. Mr. Akand returns for his dermatology review, reporting persistent spots on his back and bothersome marks left behind after previous pimples. He works as an office cleaner and notes that his skin flared up significantly after using a heavy face cream bought from a local shop in Rampura. He washes his face frequently but feels disheartened by the ongoing breakouts. He denies any systemic symptoms or joint pains. On examination: about 30 inflamed spots on the face and upper back, BP 119/84 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 91 kg. Lesions comprise a mix of papules, pustules, and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued for topical acne preparations. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and strictly avoid squeezing the spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Mitu Dewan, 74, female. Mrs. Dewan attends for her respiratory follow-up, reporting a long history of smoking, audible wheezing when walking short distances, and producing more sputum than usual. She is a homemaker and explains that her breathing symptoms worsened during the dusty dry season in Keraniganj. She reports using her inhalers regularly but struggles on humid days. She denies chest pain, orthopnoea, or ankle swelling. On examination: SpO2 86%, BP 131/83 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 78 kg. Chest examination shows diffuse ronchi and diminished breath sounds bilaterally. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued for nebulizer therapy and oral medications. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke exposure, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Emon Majumder, 79, male. Mr. Majumder presents for his first consultation, complaining of upper digestive symptoms that are much worse when lying down, a persistent sour taste in his mouth, and a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals. He works as a homemaker and notes his discomfort became worse after weeks of eating fried snacks at local tea stalls in Cox's Bazar. Presentation note: he also reports a long-standing dry cough and hoarse voice with little typical heartburn. He denies difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss. On examination: BMI 26.6, BP 114/70 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 49 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness on deep palpation. Comorbidity: Bronchial asthma. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued for acid suppression therapy. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of his bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Ziaur Sarkar, 42, male. Mr. Sarkar comes in for his first visit, reporting a twisted ankle and sharp pain when attempting to walk. He is a madrasa teacher and explains that the injury happened while stepping off a crowded bus in Wari. Presentation note: he notes that the pain is felt mainly on the top of his foot rather than directly on the ankle joint. He denies any inability to bear weight immediately after the incident or numbness in the toes. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 121/77 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 52 kg. There is mild localized swelling over the dorsum of the foot and lateral ligament complex, with intact distal neurovascular status. Comorbidity: Hypothyroidism. Assessment: Ankle sprain. Plan: a prescription was issued for analgesia and anti-inflammatory medication. He was advised to follow rest, ice, compression, and elevation for 48 hours and use a crepe bandage. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Rozina Molla, 22, female. Ms. Molla returns for her gynaecological review, reporting irregular menstrual cycles and persistent acne affecting her confidence. She works as a software developer and mentions that these concerns prompted her to seek medical evaluation after a friend in Tangail suggested testing. She denies excessive facial hair growth, sudden weight fluctuations, or pelvic pain. On examination: BMI 26.3, BP 127/77 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 65 kg. Skin inspection confirms mild facial acne, with no signs of Cushingoid features. Comorbidity: Hypothyroidism. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued to help regulate her cycle. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-09-14 03:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Arif Sheikh, 66, male. Mr. Sheikh attends for a follow-up consultation, complaining of ongoing worry about sleep, trouble falling asleep most nights, and waking up feeling completely tired.
